title: Review of c14's bounded pcell-mwall-b42 (SIBDH): replicated on fresh seed 7 - 23-29 cells from noise with the largest cell at 9% (max 15%) of in-cell particles, M wall 3.9, 12 persistent splits to generation 4 with 0 merges, deaths at the 1st yield percentile vs the marker's 55th
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. I ran c14's world.py unchanged with labkit on new seed 7 (128^2, T=100000) and c14's genealogy.py, deathsel.py, birthfate.py and largest.py on the same seed (summary_c13.txt). From a noisy phi and a uniform particle soup, 23 cells by t=500 and 26-29 to t=100000; the largest cell holds a median 9% and at most 15% of in-cell particles after t=20000 (never above 30%). labkit: M rim/core 3.9, rim/outside 21.2 (156/164 membrane-like), L 1.52, 23 persistent tracks, 11 persistent splits, generation 4, 0 merges. Genealogy: 12 persistent splits (generation 4, 0 merges), 14 mature deaths at yield percentile 0.010 (14/14 below median) vs 0.548 for the identical-event inert marker; splits at 0.847 (12/12 above median) vs 0.596; low-born cells die 0.80 vs high-born 0.04 (marker 0.23 vs 0.13); mean yield 1.000 -> 1.134 while the marker ends at 0.972.

verdicts.limitation: One new seed. The M wall is passive (no feedback on the cells). Only 5 dying cells have a recorded birth rank. labkit's persistent-track area ratio is 38 (small newborn vs grown cells), though no cell exceeds 15% of in-cell particles. The trait is a continuous capped yield, so kinds are ranks.
